summary: myseliasan now embeds each managed node's real mymatasan camera pages (Live View with relay video/PTZ/audio, Detection, Recordings, Settings) directly inside the control plane, driven entirely over the existing node-dialed control and media channels so the browser never talks to the node directly. The camera tabs reuse mymatasan's actual React components (copied into components/nodecam/, routed via a proxy apiBase + CSRF fetch shim) and mymatasan's actual stylesheet (imported via a new @mymatasan webpack alias, injected once and CSS-scoped under .nodecam-embed) so the embedded pages track mymatasan's design automatically on future builds. New cross-node Live Views wall and a node dashboard mirroring mymatasan's own analytics dashboard were added, plus per-section version banners so an older node shows a clear notice instead of a silent blank panel. Because recorded clips can be larger than the control channel's 16 MiB per-message cap and encrypted/HEVC clips aren't seekable end-to-end, mymatasan's recording download endpoint now serves HTTP Range requests (materializing a seekable decrypted/transcoded temp copy on first touch), the node's tunnel dispatcher forwards all response headers (not just Content-Type), and myseliasan exposes a new GET /api/nodes/{id}/recording-stream/{segId} endpoint that chunks each browser Range request under the tunnel's message cap and returns 206 Partial Content, enabling seekable recording playback through the embedded Recordings tab. Also fixed a dashboard request-storm caused by unstable effect dependencies and stopped index.html from being browser-cached (it references content-hashed bundle filenames, so a stale cached copy could keep a browser on an old bundle after a rebuild).
compatibility: No database schema changes. Existing mymatasan installs are unaffected for normal (non-Range) clip downloads and browser live view; the Range-serving path is additive and only engaged by Range requests. Existing myseliasan installs gain the new nav tree camera sub-branches, Live Views page, and node dashboard automatically after upgrade; no config changes are required. Recording playback through the tunnel requires the adopted node to be running a build that serves Range on the segment-download endpoint and forwards all response headers over the control channel — an older node instead shows a 'not streamable over the link' notice for tunneled playback (direct playback on the node itself, and live view/detection/settings, are unaffected). Materialized playback temp copies are written under the OS temp directory on the node and are plaintext for up to one hour before automatic cleanup; this is a deliberate trade-off to enable seekable playback of otherwise-encrypted footage over the tunnel.
